source_review.notes: Checked current or explicitly versioned official Apache Iceberg specification, schema, evolution, and Spark DDL documentation; Delta Lake column mapping, type widening, batch, protocol-feature, and change-data-feed documentation; Apache Hudi schema-evolution documentation; Apache Avro and Parquet specifications; and Protocol Buffers compatibility guidance. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Product-specific capabilities and limitations are attributed and separated from general identity and resolution principles.

evidence: Reviewed schema IDs, retained file set, writer and reader schemas, resolution rho, stable field identity, semantic type domains, conversion functions, client capability sets, required features, schema cohorts, and null/default/cast/reject counts.
Checked universal file-resolution condition, capability subset condition, injective widening requirement, and typed conversion notation.
Checked that logical schema, physical file schema, writer schema, reader projection, protocol version, and schema epoch remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Compatibility claims name the reader/writer direction, client population, schema cohort, and semantic obligations.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced account_id=42, account_type=long, region=null, note_visible=no, and reused_id=no.
Checked that decimal(10,2) has eight integer digits and decimal(12,4) also has eight, so increased total precision and scale do not imply increased integer range.
Checked boundary-test examples for integer widening, absent-field resolution, old four-byte bounds, and parsing variants without turning samples into universal proofs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal rollout duration, sample size, null rate, backfill rate, client percentage, or migration threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified identity preservation under rename/reorder and non-reuse after drop using distinct stable IDs.
Verified widening obligations require a defined injective conversion over the admitted source domain plus preservation of comparison, equality, ordering, and hashing where relevant.
Verified add-field resolution, mixed-schema canonical projection, and rollout safety arguments with explicit default, capability, stale-writer, and new-file rollback conditions.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Metadata-only evolution is proven only under format-specific resolution rules and the supported client capability set.

evidence: Reviewed add/drop/rename/reorder, name reuse, requiredness, read versus write defaults, nested structs/lists/maps, null versus absent, and map-key equality.

Reviewed integer precision, decimal precision/scale, string parsing, local/UTC timestamp semantics, historical statistics encodings, unknown metrics, partition/delete/index dependencies, and retained sensitive bytes.
Reviewed stale writers, old readers, long-running streams, CDC, feature activation, rollback after new encodings, automatic typo fields, mixed snapshots, and unsupported recovery tools.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unsupported required semantics fail explicitly; uninterpretable optional statistics weaken pruning rather than exclude files.

evidence: Traced stable field identities through table schemas, file mappings, manifests/statistics, partition specs, delete files, projections, CDC tracking, caches, and connectors.
Checked every retained file remains bound to its writer schema and resolves deterministically to the snapshot reader schema without ID reuse or ordinal guessing.
Checked schema publication, protocol requirements, concurrent writer refresh, schema epochs, migration reconciliation, retained rollback state, and audit lineage.
invariant_checking.notes: Physical deletion, semantic backfill, and incompatible conversion are not represented as simple metadata drops or defaults.

evidence: Reviewed identity-preservation, value-widening, add-field resolution, mixed-schema equivalence, and rollout safety arguments.
Checked counterexamples for position/name binding, ID reuse, lossy numeric changes, timezone reinterpretation, count-only migration validation, and schema-pointer-only rollback.
Checked the verification matrix spans historical/current/mixed files, old/new clients, boundaries, streams, CDC, stale commits, protocol rejection, and recovery.
proof_review.notes: Sampling is labeled empirical confidence; universal value-fit claims require constraints or complete relevant-domain evidence.

evidence: Audited logical/physical/writer/reader schema, field identity, resolution, promotion, widening, narrowing, reinterpretation, and rewrite terminology.
Confirmed absent, null, initial/read default, write default, materialized backfill, cast failure, and rejected record are distinguished.
Confirmed backward, forward, and full compatibility; schema versus protocol version; metadata-only versus rewrite evolution; and technical versus business compatibility are separate claims.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current product features are labeled by their documented version and capability requirements.

evidence: Reviewed files/bytes by writer schema, stale-writer rejection, resolution fallback, unknown statistics, casts, overflow, null/default provenance, client incompatibility, CDC lag, rewrite progress, reconciliation, and rollback readiness.
Confirmed evidence is segmented by snapshot, schema ID, stable field ID, operation, client/version, file cohort, and boundary value where relevant.
Confirmed one current-engine read, recent-file sample, row-count match, successful DDL, or protocol flag is not mislabeled as ecosystem-wide compatibility proof.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Canary results support rollout decisions but do not replace historical fixtures and supported-client coverage.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed logical/physical resolution, stable identity, additive and non-additive changes, defaults and requiredness, type domains, nested collections, historical statistics, dependencies, protocol clients, concurrency, rewrite migration, observability, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable schema inventories, field mappings, client capability gates, stale-writer commit validation, stream epochs, automatic-evolution policy, boundary profiling, golden files, dual reads, keyed reconciliation, canaries, backfill, cutover, rollback, metrics, audit, and explicit unsupported-client failure. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from schema identities and resolution through change classification, value preservation, dependent metadata, distributed rollout, and rewrite migration. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover rename, widening, defaults, typo quarantine, decimals, timestamps, delete dependencies, stale streams, parsing migration, executable ID resolution, ID reuse, required rollout, bounds decoding, and client matrices.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Iceberg/Delta Lake/Hudi/Avro/Parquet/Protobuf maintainer, schema-registry or query-engine implementer, database/distributed-systems/storage/platform/streaming/CDC/security specialist, data owner, production operator, affected consumer, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
